note: Transactions that state their own nature. 'LOAN REPAYMENT' is not a merchant and not a channel — it is the transaction telling you what it is, and after a tax invoice it is the strongest evidence available. On the real Standard Bank statement 33 rows are classified this way and were correct; they had been sitting anonymously inside a keyword table with no name for what made them trustworthy.
why_this_is_different_from_a_merchant: A merchant name says WHO. This says WHAT. 'SHELL' could be fuel, a pie or a car wash, so the name cannot settle the category. 'INSURANCE PREMIUM' can only be an insurance premium, whoever collected it — which is why this evidence carries a higher grade than merchant recognition and why it needs no discriminator.
bank_agnostic: Every South African bank prints these words. Nothing here is keyed to a bank profile, and nothing here should be — a term that only one bank uses is bank wording, and belongs in channel_lexicon.json.

deliberately_absent.salary: 'SALARY' in a reference is often the payer's description of a transfer to a person, not proof of employment. It needs corroboration and belongs to reasoning, not to self-description.
deliberately_absent.rent: The word appears in trading names ('Rent-A-Car'). Boundary matching alone would not make it safe.
deliberately_absent.fee: Handled by the bank-charge evidence path, which is stronger because the BANK named it on its own statement.
deliberately_absent.transfer: A mechanism, not a nature. Lives in banking_semantics.json.
